findings.message: `readOrUnknown` turns any failed read of a change's files into a parsed change with phase `?` and `approved: false`. Failures it catches include a rejected `$.fs.read` or `$.fs.stat`, a rejected `$.fs.exists`, and a non-string read. The gate then runs on that snapshot and returns a definite verdict. In `block` mode it denies the edit with "no approved change is open". R2 says a gate read failure must show a toast and allow the edit. Here the read failure blocks work instead, and the message wrongly claims that no approval exists. Fix: record that a change was unreadable, for example with an `isUnreadable` flag on the change or the snapshot, keeping the `?` row for the pane. In `gateDecision`, treat an unreadable change as a gate failure: throw into the existing catch so it shows the toast and allows the edit. Do not count it as not approved. Add a variant test that drives the real `tool.call` path with three failures: `fs.read` rejects, `fs.stat` rejects, and `fs.read` returns a non-string, each on an approved change's `state.json`. Each row must assert that the tool ran and the toast was shown.
findings.scenario: Gate in `block` mode. `/x/.specclaw/changes/001-a/state.json` records an approved proposal, but `$.fs.read` on that file rejects (EACCES or EBUSY). A Write to `/x/src/a.ts` returns `{ deny: 'specclaw: no approved change is open…' }`. R2 expects a toast and the edit to run.

findings.message: `realPathOf` uses `.catch(() => undefined)`, so every `$.fs.stat` failure, including EACCES and EIO, is read as "this path does not exist". `placePath` then walks up to an ancestor and builds the target from the unresolved names. A symbolic link whose stat fails is therefore compared by its text, not by where it points. The gate can then decide the file is outside the project and allow the edit with no toast, which R2 forbids. Fix: map only ENOENT/ENOTDIR to `undefined` and rethrow every other error, so it reaches the gate's catch and its toast. Add table rows to `place.test.ts` where `fs.stat` throws a non-ENOENT error on a link into the project, for example `/link/src/a.ts` and `/link/new/a.ts`.
findings.scenario: `/link` is a symbolic link to `/repo` (the cwd) and no change is approved. `$.fs.stat('/link/src/a.ts', {resolve:true})` and the stat of each ancestor below `/` reject with EACCES. The walk stops at `/`, giving target `/link/src/a.ts`, which is outside `/repo`, so the verdict is ALLOW. The Write lands in `/repo/src/a.ts` and no toast is shown.

findings.message: A failed `$.command.register` is dropped silently with `.catch(() => undefined)`. `/specclaw-pane` is then missing and nothing tells the user why. Show a toast or status note when registration fails.

The post-tool refresh-failure rows check the run count and the tool result, but not what the user sees. `events.test.ts` asserts the status `specclaw: could not read changes` for the other hooks, but this path has no such check. If this handler stopped using `refreshQuietly`, these tests would stay green. Add the same `ui.status` assertion here.
